LESSON: ANIMALS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 1.2: Animals
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Animals, part of Living Things and their Environment in Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY.

Key inquiry question: Why are animals grouped as living things?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. take a walk in the school compound and adjacent environment to observe, discuss and record evidence that animals: feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond to changes in their environment and die,

2. search for information from print and non- print materials on characteristics of animals as living things and discuss the findings with peers,

3. search for information from print and non- print materials on main differences between vertebrates and invertebrates and share with peers,

4. take a walk in the school compound and immediate environment to identify vertebrates and invertebrates in their locality. Note: Learners observe safety precautions and take care of animals during the learning activities.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. take a walk in the school compound and adjacent environment to observe, discuss and record evidence that animals: feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond to changes in their environment and die,
2. search for information from print and non- print materials on characteristics of animals as living things and discuss the findings with peers,
3. search for information from print and non- print materials on main differences between vertebrates and invertebrates and share with peers,
4. take a walk in the school compound and immediate environment to identify vertebrates and invertebrates in their locality. Note: Learners observe safety precautions and take care of animals during the learning activities.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Animals together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: The learner contributes to group decision making by participating actively as they discuss

characteristics of animals as living things.

● Creativity and Imagination: The learner discovers new ways of solving problems of keeping records as they design and make a

portfolio of vertebrates and invertebrates.

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner takes care of the different materials they use as they search for information from print and non-print

materials on main differences between vertebrates and invertebrates and share with peers.

• Respect: The learner appreciates divergent ideas from peers as they discuss their findings on characteristics of animals as living

things.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Animal welfare: The learner takes care of animals during the learning activities.

● Safety and security: The learner observes safety when handling animals.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

Agriculture and Nutrition: The learner uses the information on characteristics of animals as living things in the study of

livestock.
